items.title: Interview #104 Andrew Moore, Co-founder & CEO of Lovelace
items.summary: Andrew Moore, Co-founder and CEO of Lovelace, breaks down why an AI answer that merely sounds right is dangerous in banks, hospitals and defense, where one question can touch hundreds of thousands of facts. He explains how an AI that read local newspapers saw a fleet of ships leaving a Chinese port for Taiwan as the start of fishing season rather than an invasion, why bigger context windows cannot keep up with problems that grow exponentially, and how a leading question lets a model build a convincing case for almost any hunch. Andrew also dives into why entity resolution and data entitlements stall more projects than the models do, and why a $25 answer has to fall to about a cent before it can run every five minutes. Finally, he shares why defense AI deserves the same years of testing as a new helicopter, and why independent corroboration is the judgment machines most need to learn.
